plates.side_label: 1891–1995 TIMELINE · DRIESCH TWINS, MANGOLD-SPEMANN ORGANIZER, LEWIS/NÜSSLEIN-VOLHARD/WIESCHAUS, 180-BP HOMEOBOX, PAX6 & 1993 SONIC HEDGEHOG DIGITS
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1891 & May 1921 (Hans Driesch shakes 2-cell sea-urchin embryos into identical twins in Naples; Hilde Mangold & Hans Spemann transplant the newt dorsal blastopore lip in Freiburg and discover the embryonic Organizer, winning the 1935 Nobel Prize) · 7 Dec 1978 & 30 Oct 1980 (Edward B. Lewis maps the colinear Bithorax complex and 4-winged Ultrabithorax fly; Christiane Nüsslein-Volhard & Eric Wieschaus map the 15 fruit-fly segmentation genes, sharing the 1995 Nobel Prize) · Mar–Jul 1984 & 24 Mar 1995 (Matthew Scott & Walter Gehring discover the conserved 180-bp Homeobox across flies, frogs, mice, and humans, and Gehring's team induces a fruit-fly eye on a fly's leg using the mouse Pax6 gene).

teach_overlay.label: 1891–1995 EMBRYO & HOX TIMELINE · DEC 1993 TABIN SONIC HEDGEHOG (SHH) LIMB-BUD GRADIENT PATTERNING PINKY TO THUMB
teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1891 → 1995) alongside Clifford Tabin's December 1993 Sonic hedgehog (SHH) Zone of Polarizing Activity gradient patterning digits 5 to 1 across nested HOXD9–HOXD13 genes
teach_overlay.scale: from a loop of baby hair in 1921 to a mouse gene inside a fruit fly in 1995, scientists proved that every animal with a head and a heart is built from the same half-billion-year-old genetic blueprint
